$comment: Single source of truth for the OPC UA MCP tool surface shared by both servers. The Node server builds its tools/list response directly from this file (copied into build/ at build time). The Python (FastMCP) server reads tool descriptions and the capability node IDs from it; its signature-derived input schemas are checked against this file by tests/test_contract_parity.py. To add or change a tool: edit this file, then update each server's per-tool logic (Node: a case in the CallTool switch; Python: the @mcp.tool function), and add an E2E test. A tool whose output is more than free text also names a shape from "resultShapes"; tests/e2e/test_contract_parity.py checks both servers' actual output against it.

resultShapes.$comment: Canonical response shapes, referenced by a tool's "resultShape". Both servers must produce the referenced shape verbatim: a client (or a model) that learns one server's output must be able to read the other's. See issue #23.

historyRecords.$comment: Returned as one MCP text content block per record, each block the JSON object described by "items". An empty result is zero blocks. The Python server additionally returns the array as structured content.

value.description: The recorded value, encoded per its OPC UA data type: numbers, booleans and strings stay themselves; a ByteString is base64; a DateTime is ISO-8601 UTC; a Guid is a lower-case UUID; NodeId, StatusCode, QualifiedName and LocalizedText are their canonical text forms; an Int64/UInt64 outside the range a JSON number can hold exactly, and a non-finite Double, become strings ("9007199254740993", "NaN"); an array value is a JSON array of those. null for an interval the server holds no data for. The full table, and the fact that both servers produce the same encoding for the same reading, is pinned by tests/fixtures/value-encoding.json.

timestamp.description: Source timestamp, ISO-8601 UTC with a trailing 'Z'. Example: '2026-09-09T13:36:01.468Z'. null when the server supplied none.

status.description: OPC UA status code name. Examples: 'Good', 'BadNoData'.

eventRecords.$comment: Returned as one MCP text content block per event, each block the JSON object described by "items". No events is zero blocks. The Python server additionally returns the array as structured content. Every field is present on every record; a field the event does not carry — the condition fields of a plain BaseEventType, say — is null. The field order and the OPC UA browse paths behind it are "events.fields" below, which is what both servers build their EventFilter select clauses from.

event_id.description: Server-assigned identifier of this event notification, base64 (it is a ByteString). Pass it back to acknowledge_alarm.

event_type.description: NodeId of the event's type, e.g. 'ns=0;i=2041' (BaseEventType) or 'ns=0;i=9341' (ExclusiveLimitAlarmType).

source_node.description: NodeId of the node the event is about.

source_name.description: Human-readable name of that source, e.g. 'Temperature'.

time.description: When the event occurred, ISO-8601 UTC with a trailing 'Z'.

message.description: The event's message text, without its locale.

condition_id.description: NodeId of the condition instance, for events that are conditions; null for a plain event. This is what acknowledge_alarm calls the Acknowledge method on.

active.description: ActiveState/Id: true while the alarm's condition is met. Null for a condition that is not an alarm.

acked.description: AckedState/Id: false until someone acknowledges the condition.

retain.description: Retain: true while the server considers the condition worth showing to an operator. list_active_alarms returns only retained conditions.

events.$comment: Alarms & Conditions wiring, shared so both servers ask the same questions of a server and name the answers the same way. The node IDs are the spec's own well-known ones (OPC UA Part 9); "fields" is both the EventFilter select clause list and the field order of "resultShapes.eventRecords". A path is a dotted OPC UA browse path relative to the event type, resolved against BaseEventType — Part 4 §7.4.4.5 says a server evaluates the path without regard to the type when the operand names BaseEventType, which is how one filter can select condition fields that a plain event does not have (they come back null). "ConditionId" is the exception the spec calls out: it is not a component of ConditionType but the NodeId attribute of the condition instance itself, so it is selected as an empty browse path against ConditionType.

defaults.$comment: The values the tool descriptions above promise, single-sourced so the two servers cannot promise the same default and apply different ones.

tools.name: read_opcua_node
tools.description: Read the value of a specific OPC UA node

node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID in the format 'ns=<namespace>;i=<identifier>'. Example: 'ns=2;i=2'.

tools.name: write_opcua_node
tools.description: Write a value to a specific OPC UA node

node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID in the format 'ns=<namespace>;i=<identifier>'. Example: 'ns=2;i=3'.

value.description: The value to write to the node. Will be converted based on node type.

tools.name: browse_opcua_node_children
tools.description: Browse the children of a specific OPC UA node

node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID to browse (e.g., 'ns=0;i=85' for Objects folder).

tools.name: read_multiple_opcua_nodes
tools.description: Read the values of multiple OPC UA nodes in a single request

node_ids.description: A list of OPC UA node IDs to read (e.g., ['ns=2;i=2', 'ns=2;i=3']).

tools.name: write_multiple_opcua_nodes
tools.description: Write values to multiple OPC UA nodes in a single request

nodes_to_write.description: A list of objects containing 'node_id' and 'value'. Example: [{'node_id': 'ns=2;i=2', 'value': '10.5'}, {'node_id': 'ns=2;i=3', 'value': 'active'}]

tools.name: call_opcua_method
tools.description: Call a method on a specific OPC UA object node

object_node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID of the object that contains the method. Example: 'ns=2;i=1' for the Methods folder.

method_node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID of the method to call. Example: 'ns=2;i=2' for StartProduction method.

arguments.description: List of arguments to pass to the method. Arguments will be converted to appropriate OPC UA variants.

tools.name: get_all_variables
tools.description: Get all available variables from the OPC UA server, excluding those under the built-in 'Server' object

tools.name: subscribe_events
tools.description: Start buffering OPC UA events (alarms, condition changes, plain events) from a notifier node. Returns at once; the events themselves are collected in the background and read with read_events. Calling this again for the same node restarts the subscription with the new settings

node_id.description: The notifier node to subscribe to. Defaults to the Server object 'ns=0;i=2253', which is where most servers publish every event they raise.

severity_min.description: Buffer only events of at least this OPC UA severity (1-1000). Default 0, which keeps every event.

buffer_size.description: How many events to hold before the oldest are dropped (default 100).

tools.name: read_events
tools.description: Read the events buffered by subscribe_events, oldest first. The events returned are removed from the buffer, so a second call returns only what has arrived since

node_id.description: The subscribed notifier node to read from, as passed to subscribe_events. Defaults to the Server object 'ns=0;i=2253'.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return (default 50).

tools.name: list_active_alarms
tools.description: List the alarm and condition instances the server is currently retaining — those that are active, unacknowledged, or both. Asks the server for them directly (the ConditionRefresh method), so the answer is the server's own current set and needs no prior subscription

node_id.description: The notifier node whose conditions to list. Defaults to the Server object 'ns=0;i=2253'.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the server to finish sending its retained conditions (default 5).

tools.name: acknowledge_alarm
tools.description: Acknowledge an alarm or condition, identified by the event_id of the event that reported it (from list_active_alarms or read_events). An acknowledgement tells the server an operator has seen the alarm; it does not clear the underlying condition

event_id.description: The 'event_id' of the event that reported the alarm, exactly as returned (base64).

comment.description: Comment to record with the acknowledgement, e.g. who is dealing with it.

condition_id.description: NodeId of the condition instance to acknowledge. Only needed when the event did not come from this server's own list_active_alarms / read_events output, which is where the condition behind an event_id is otherwise remembered from.

tools.name: read_history_opcua_node
tools.description: Read the historical values of a specific OPC UA node

node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID in the format 'ns=<namespace>;i=<identifier>'. Example: 'ns=2;i=2'.

num_values.description: Number of values to read (default: unlimited)

tools.name: read_aggregate_opcua_node
tools.description: Calculate the historical aggregates over a defined time range, divided into smaller chunks defined by the `processing_interval` (in milliseconds). The server divides the [`start_time`, `end_time`] domain into these intervals, returning one aggregated value per interval

node_id.description: The OPC UA node ID in the format 'ns=<namespace>;i=<identifier>'. Example: 'ns=2;i=2'.

processing_interval.description: The duration (ms) for each computed value. If set to 0, the server calculates a single aggregate value for the entire range.
